lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In the northern kingdom of Israel, King Ahab had turned away from the LORD. Queen Jezebel had promoted the worship of Baal, and the nation was being led deeper into idolatry.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then Elijah the Tishbite appeared before Ahab. He came with a warning from the living God.

lines.speaker: elijah
lines.text: As surely as the LORD, the God of Israel, lives—the God I serve—there will be no dew or rain unless the LORD gives the word.

choices.label: Stand boldly on God's word
choices.note: Elijah's message is clear: Israel's drought is a direct challenge to Baal, the god they claimed controlled the rain.

choices.label: Feel the weight of the king's threat
choices.note: Elijah is brave, but the story will soon show that even a courageous prophet can become afraid.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Leave here. Go east and hide beside the Kerith Ravine. You will drink from the brook, and I have commanded ravens to provide food for you there.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Elijah obeyed. Morning and evening the ravens brought him bread and meat, and he drank from the brook.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But after a time the brook dried up. The drought had reached even the place where God had provided for Elijah.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Go at once to Zarephath in Sidon. I have directed a widow there to provide for you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At the town gate Elijah found a widow gathering sticks. She was preparing what she believed would be the last meal for herself and her son.

lines.speaker: elijah
lines.text: Please bring me a little water—and while you are going, bring me a small piece of bread.

choices.label: Trust God's promise
choices.note: The widow is asked to trust before she can see the provision.

choices.label: Hold on to what little remains
choices.note: Her fear is understandable. She has almost nothing left, yet God's provision is about to become visible.

lines.speaker: widow
lines.text: I have no bread. Only a handful of flour and a little oil. I was gathering sticks to prepare one final meal for my son and me.

lines.speaker: elijah
lines.text: Do not be afraid. The LORD says the flour will not run out and the oil will not fail until rain returns to the land.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She trusted the word of the LORD. Day after day there was enough flour and oil for Elijah, the widow, and her household.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then tragedy struck: the widow's son became ill and died. Elijah carried the boy upstairs, prayed to the LORD, and pleaded for his life.

lines.speaker: elijah
lines.text: LORD my God, let this child's life return to him.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The LORD heard Elijah's prayer. The child's life returned, and Elijah brought him back to his mother.

lines.speaker: widow
lines.text: Now I know that you are a man of God and that the word of the LORD from your mouth is true.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: After a long drought, the LORD told Elijah to show himself to Ahab. The time had come to announce that rain would return.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Ahab's official Obadiah had secretly protected a hundred prophets of the LORD from Jezebel. But now Elijah stood openly before the king.

lines.speaker: elijah
lines.text: Gather all Israel on Mount Carmel. Bring the prophets of Baal. Let the people see who truly answers prayer.

lines.speaker: elijah
lines.text: How long will you keep wavering? If the LORD is God, follow him. If Baal is God, follow him.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The prophets of Baal cried out from morning until noon. They called, shouted, and performed their rituals—but there was no answer.

lines.speaker: elijah
lines.text: Cry louder! Perhaps your god is busy, travelling, or asleep and needs to be awakened.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then Elijah repaired the LORD's broken-down altar. He used twelve stones, one for each tribe of Israel, and had the sacrifice and wood soaked with water.

lines.speaker: elijah
lines.text: LORD, God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel, show today that you are God in Israel and that I am your servant. Answer me, LORD!

choices.label: Pray with confidence
choices.note: Elijah's prayer is not a performance. He asks God to turn the people's hearts back to him.

choices.label: Remember who must receive the glory
choices.note: The sign is meant to reveal the LORD—not to make Elijah famous.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then the fire of the LORD fell. It consumed the sacrifice, the wood, the stones, the soil, and even the water in the trench.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The people fell facedown and cried out: The LORD—he is God! The LORD—he is God!

lines.speaker: elijah
lines.text: Go back and look toward the sea. The drought is ending.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A small cloud appeared. The sky grew dark, the wind rose, and soon the land was filled with rain.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: When Jezebel heard what had happened on Mount Carmel, she sent Elijah a deadly threat.

lines.speaker: jezebel
lines.text: By tomorrow, I will make your life like the lives of the prophets you have defeated!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Elijah was afraid. The prophet who had stood before Ahab now ran into the wilderness for his life.

lines.speaker: elijah
lines.text: I have had enough, LORD. Take my life. I am no better than my ancestors.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Exhausted, Elijah lay down beneath a broom bush and fell asleep. An angel touched him and told him to eat.

lines.speaker: angel
lines.text: Get up and eat, for the journey is too much for you.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The angel came again with food and water. Strengthened by it, Elijah travelled forty days and forty nights to Horeb, the mountain of God.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At Horeb, Elijah entered a cave and spent the night. God asked him a question that reached beyond the storm outside.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: What are you doing here, Elijah?

lines.speaker: elijah
lines.text: I have been zealous for the LORD. Israel has broken your covenant, destroyed your altars, and killed your prophets. I am the only one left, and they are trying to kill me too.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Go out and stand on the mountain. The LORD is about to pass by.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A powerful wind tore at the mountain. But the LORD was not in the wind. Then came an earthquake—but the LORD was not in the earthquake.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then came fire. But the LORD was not in the fire. After the fire came a gentle whisper.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: When Elijah heard it, he covered his face with his cloak and stood at the entrance of the cave.

choices.label: Listen for God in the quiet
choices.note: Elijah discovers that God's presence is not limited to spectacular signs. The quiet voice matters too.

choices.label: Expect another great sign
choices.note: Elijah has seen fire, rain, wind, and earthquakes. Now the story turns his attention from spectacle to listening.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Go back. Anoint Hazael king over Aram, Jehu king over Israel, and Elisha to succeed you as prophet. And remember: I have kept seven thousand in Israel who have not bowed to Baal.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Later, Ahab wanted Naboth's vineyard because it was beside the king's palace. Naboth refused to sell the inheritance that belonged to his family.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Jezebel arranged false accusations against Naboth. He was condemned and killed, and Ahab took possession of the vineyard.

lines.speaker: god
lines.text: Go down to meet Ahab in Naboth's vineyard. He has gone there to take possession of it.

lines.speaker: elijah
lines.text: This is what the LORD says: You have murdered Naboth and taken his land. Because you have given yourself to evil, judgment is coming upon your house.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Elijah's ministry was not only about miracles. He also confronted kings when power was used to crush the innocent.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The time came for the LORD to take Elijah up to heaven in a whirlwind. Elijah and Elisha travelled together from Gilgal.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At the Jordan, Elijah struck the water with his cloak. The river divided, and they crossed on dry ground.

lines.speaker: elijah
lines.text: Tell me what I can do for you before I am taken from you.

lines.speaker: elisha
lines.text: Please let me inherit a double portion of your spirit.

lines.speaker: elijah
lines.text: You have asked for something difficult. Yet if you see me when I am taken from you, it will be granted.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Suddenly a chariot of fire and horses of fire appeared. They separated Elijah and Elisha, and Elijah was carried up into heaven in a whirlwind.

lines.speaker: elisha
lines.text: My father! My father! The chariots and horsemen of Israel!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Elisha picked up Elijah's cloak. The prophetic mission did not end—it passed to the next generation.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The story of Elijah ends with a prophet taken from the earth, but God's work continues through Elisha.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: THE END
